title: structured output: add CFG + regex constrained decoding backends and tokenizer edgecase handling
author: Aditi Rao
merge_outcome: merged after addressing tokenizer fallback edgecases and updating compatibility layer
description: Add two new constrained decoding backends (CFG/grammar and regex) and robust tokenizer edgecase handling to improve structured-output reliability and OpenAI-compat behavior. Motivation: downstream integrations rely on strict JSON/CFG outputs (function/tool calling, structured responses) and we saw recurring production failures when tokenization splits constraint tokens across byte sequences or when regex constraints hit unicode/emoji edgecases. This PR implements: 1) A CFG backend that compiles a context-free grammar into a prefix-acceptor optimized for incremental streaming; 2) A regex backend that supports anchored and capturing-pattern constraints with safe incremental matching; 3) Tokenizer-aware constraint mapping layer that aligns byte/utf8 boundaries and falls back to unicode-aware regexes when tokenizer splits would otherwise invalidate constraints; 4) Integration with the OpenAI compatibility layer so function-calling examples continue to work when constrained decoding is enabled; 5) New unit and integration tests covering surrogate pairs, combining marks, zero-width joiners, and tokenizer boundary splits; 6) Benchmarks and perf tweaks to keep latency impact < 5% for common request sizes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and linear tasks (ENG-1423) - [x] Implement CFG backend and streaming acceptor - [x] Implement regex backend with incremental engine - [x] Tokenizer alignment and unicode fallback heuristics - [x] OpenAI compatibility tests updated - [x] CI coverage and perf benchmarks added - [x] Docs and API surface notes updated (redwood-docs) Related: ENG-1478 covers rollout/feature flag gating and Dedicated autoscale considerations. See comments below for reviewer feedback and fixes performed.

release_notes: Structured output: added new constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) and improved tokenizer edgecase handling. This enables more reliable function/tool calling and structured responses for Unicode-heavy inputs. No breaking changes. Feature is behind a feature flag for Dedicated/Private clusters. See docs/structured-output.md for usage and migration notes.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature is gated behind `constrained_decoding_v2` flag. Recommend staged rollout: start on hosted with 1% traffic, monitor structured-output regression alerts and tokenization error rates for 72h, then expand. Dedicated customers must opt-in due to tokenizer/runtime differences.
testing_summary: Added 28 unit tests and 6 integration scenarios. CI matrix runs on linux/mac and with OpenAI-compat adapter toggled. Observed intermittent flake on one integration test fixed by increasing mock buffering timeout. All checks green on final run.
perf_summary: Median latency regression ~3% for constrained decoding enabled on typical 128-token requests. Tail p95 increase ~4.8%. Memory overhead bounded by compiled grammar size; default guard prevents >200k nodes.
security_implications: No new network surface. Rejects overly large grammars to prevent OOM. Regex backend uses safe incremental engine to avoid catastrophic backtracking.
notes: This PR also touches the OpenAI compatibility layer to keep function-calling behavior consistent. Docs updated with examples showing how to enable constrained decoding in the Python/TS SDKs.
